name: Soudan 2
summary: A historical fine-grained calorimeter in Minnesota provided an independent atmospheric-neutrino measurement using a detector technology distinct from water Cherenkov experiments.
detection_principle: Charged particles ionised gas in drift tubes embedded in corrugated iron. Drift time and anode/cathode readout reconstructed tracks and showers, while an external active shield rejected entering backgrounds.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The laboratory history records the experiment as ending in 2001.

collaboration.name: Soudan 2 Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Segmentation
key_parameters.value: 224 calorimeter modules of approximately 4.3 tonnes each

key_parameters.name: Readout
key_parameters.value: Approximately 1 m long, 15 mm internal-diameter drift tubes

results.summary: The final 5.90 fiducial kilotonne-year atmospheric sample showed muon-neutrino oscillation effects in its L/E distribution.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
